answer: Answers are compared against a hidden reference set of 3 accepted mechanisms and scored on how much new ground they cover rather than on how closely they match. Because the summit reference is updated at each signal checkpoint, coverage is the scarce resource, and the jade audit records how much each answer added. Repeating an already-covered mechanism thus earns nothing extra, so one template cannot pay for 113 aliases however many keys the operator holds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
